top_choice_rationale: P001 honours a distinct, mature invention: the magic-wavelength condition removes the trap-induced light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once, and lattice clocks have been reproduced and intercompared across independent laboratories near 1e-18. The two-name allocation (Katori for the concept, Ye for taking the platform to the accuracy frontier) is defensible, and a species-neutral citation naming the magic-wavelength lattice separates it from the comb and ion-control prizes. The convergence of the committee is partly the result of members moving after reading each other, so I re-tested the argument independently and it holds. No award is a clearly inferior outcome to a well-supported achievement.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my instrument work (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO+, XL-Calibur) is in astroparticle physics and has no documented tie to Katori, Ye or optical clocks
